title: One key is the agent
lede: Agent Registry mints an agent access key: one credential that IS the agent. Scopes, allowed models, RPM/TPM/budget, expiry, guardrail and reachable apps all hang off the key. No sign-in, no token exchange.

nodes.label: Select Agentic Apps
sub: MCP grant can list tools; rest refused

nodes.label: LLM provider door
sub: Privilege holds the real provider key
agent holds a virtual key only

steps.title: Mint the identity
steps.what: The key is minted with scopes (llm / mcp / a2a), allowed models, RPM/TPM and budget caps, expiry, a guardrail and a custodian — the named human the agent acts as. If the custodian's account goes inactive, the key stops working.

steps.title: The grant comes from selection
steps.what: Selecting Agentic Apps on the key is the grant: saving auto-creates a policy. For MCP apps the grant can list tools; the other tools are hidden and refused.

steps.title: LLM keys hold a virtual key
steps.what: One provider per key, with a model allowlist and rate/budget caps. Privilege holds the real provider key and injects it server-side, so the agent only ever holds a virtual key.

steps.title: The agent calls with the key
steps.what: The agent sends Authorization: Bearer <key> — no sign-in, no token exchange. The key IS the agent.

steps.title: The gateway checks everything
steps.what: Scope, app and tool against the grant, rate and budget caps enforced natively, and the per-key AI Guard runtime step. Revoke (Revoked: true) is the instant non-destructive kill.
